# ACORD form automation: 12 questions agencies ask before they buy


Abhi Balijepalli


Co-founder, CopyCat


Published November 23, 2026


·


10 min read


The short version


- Good ACORD form automation reads the account’s documents and fills every form in the submission from one read: the ACORD 125, the line sections and the schedules.
- Every value should show the page it came from, and anything the documents don’t answer should be flagged, never guessed.
- At renewal, last year’s answers should carry forward into the boxes this year’s documents leave empty, each marked as coming from last year.
- The finished forms should stay editable and land back in your agency management system.
- [CopyCat ACORD Submissions](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-form-automation) does all of this for commercial agencies. We make it, so hold it to the same questions as any other tool.


Account managers repeat the same job every renewal: retyping names, addresses, class codes, vehicles, drivers and five years of losses into one ACORD after another. ACORD form automation software promises to take that work away, but the products sold under that label do very different things. This guide is built around the questions agencies ask when they evaluate one. Each answer says what to look for and how CopyCat handles it.


We make CopyCat, so our answers about it are not independent. For a side-by-side of seven tools, read[Best AI for ACORD form filling](https://www.runcopycat.com/blog/best-ai-for-acord-form-filling) .


## 1. What types of ACORD form software are there?


Five kinds of product are sold as ACORD software. Decide which one you need before you compare vendors.


Type What it does Good fit when Examples


Forms library in your AMS Prints ACORD forms from the client record The client record is complete and current Most agency management systems


Client-completed digital applications Sends the insured an online questionnaire and turns the answers into ACORDs The client will actually finish it Indio, Broker Buddha


One-off PDF fillers Fills one fillable PDF from data you provide You fill a few forms now and then Instafill.ai


Document-to-ACORD AI Reads the account’s documents and fills the whole submission The answers sit in dec pages, loss runs, MVRs and last year’s apps CopyCat, Cooper


ACORD data extraction Reads values out of ACORDs that arrive You are a carrier, MGA or wholesaler receiving submissions FurtherAI, Docsumo


Most commercial agencies want the fourth kind. The information already exists in documents, and the work is moving it onto the forms.


## 2. Can it fill every ACORD in a submission from one set of documents?


It should. The insured’s name, FEIN, addresses, locations and drivers repeat across the[ACORD 125](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-125) ,[126](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-126) ,[127](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-127) and[140](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-140) . A tool that fills one form at a time makes you check the same facts four times.


In CopyCat you drop the documents once, pick the lines of business and the forms, and one build fills them all: the 125 application, each line section, the vehicle and driver schedules ([129](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-129) and[163](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-163) ) and state supplements such as the[137](https://www.runcopycat.com/acord-forms/acord-137) . Remarks that run out of room continue onto an additional remarks page automatically.


## 3. What documents can it read? What about client emails and scans?


Look for a tool that takes whatever the client sent, in any order, with no templates to map. CopyCat reads last year’s ACORDs and carrier applications, dec pages and policies, quotes, loss runs, statements of values, MVRs, vehicle and driver spreadsheets and intake notes. Scanned or digital PDFs, Word files, Excel workbooks and photos all work, and you can add the client’s website for the description of operations.


When a submission arrives by email, save the attachments and drop them in, then give the assistant anything the client wrote in the body of the email.


## 4. Does it show where each value came from?


This decides whether an account manager trusts the output. Without a source, checking a FEIN or a VIN means opening every document again. CopyCat cites every value it pulls to its page, such as “Loss runs, p. 3” or “Schedule, Vehicles”. Click the citation and the page opens next to the submission.


## 5. What happens when the documents don’t answer a question?


The safe behavior is a blank that is marked for review. A plausible guess at a year built, a square footage or a prior loss is how E&O problems start. CopyCat leaves those fields for you, lists them, and never invents an answer to make a form look complete. Give the assistant the answer, or add a document that has it, and the forms update.


## 6. Can we edit the filled PDF without breaking the form layout?


You should be able to fix a value on the ACORD itself, not in a side panel you then re-export. CopyCat opens the filled forms in an editor that looks like the PDF. Click any field to change it, tick or clear a box, or ask the assistant to change a value everywhere it appears (“revenue is $4.2M now”), with an Undo. When you are done, download the finished PDFs, or fillable copies with every field still live for anyone who needs to make a late change.


## 7. Does it reuse last year’s ACORDs at renewal?


Renewal applications are mostly the same as last year, which is why retyping them is so frustrating. Upload last year’s ACORDs with this year’s dec pages and loss runs. CopyCat fills the new forms from the facts in this year’s documents first, then copies a fillable prior ACORD field for field into the boxes still empty. Your own edits always win. Each carried value is cited to the prior form’s page, so you can see which answers came from last year and confirm the ones that may have changed, such as the yes or no questions. A printed or scanned prior ACORD is read like any other document.


## 8. Does it work with our agency management system?


Ask two things: can it read the client record, and can it file the finished forms back? CopyCat connects to HawkSoft and AMS360. Link the submission to the client and CopyCat imports the client record and in-force policies as a cited source, then files the finished ACORDs and filled carrier supplements back on the client when you send them. Agencies on Applied Epic, EZLynx or another system download the PDFs and attach them the way they do today.


## 9. Can it fill carrier supplements too?


Carriers often want their own questionnaire with the ACORDs: a contractor supplement, a trucking supplement, a banquet hall questionnaire. Upload it with the documents and ask the assistant to fill it. CopyCat answers it from the same facts as the ACORDs, whether it is a fillable PDF or a printed form saved as a PDF.


## 10. Can it handle many accounts at once?


“Batch” means two different things. Filling several forms for one account is the normal case (question 2). Working through many separate accounts is a queue. In CopyCat each submission is one account, builds run on CopyCat’s servers, and an account manager can start the next account while the last one builds. Every submission keeps its own documents, forms and history.


## 11. Which ACORD editions does it fill?


Underwriters expect the current layout. CopyCat is a member of ACORD and fills current editions, including the ACORD 125 and 126 (2025/03) and the ACORD 130 (2026/08). A submission keeps the edition its forms were picked with, so a form never changes layout halfway through.


## 12. What does it cost, and can we try it first?


Ask for the price model, the contract length, and whether new forms and editions cost extra. ACORD Submissions is part of[CopyCat Pro](https://www.runcopycat.com/pricing) , quoted on team size and usage after a demo, with monthly plans that cancel anytime. To try it, bring one of your own messy accounts to a 15-minute demo and we fill the ACORDs live from your documents.


## Contract terms worth checking


Term What to ask


Data use Are your client documents used to train AI models? CopyCat does not train on customer documents.


Editions Who updates the forms when ACORD releases a new edition, and does it cost extra?


Exports Can you download fillable PDFs, so the forms stay yours if you leave?


AMS write-back Which systems can it file the finished forms to, and is that in the plan you are quoted?


Commitment Monthly or annual, and what happens to your data when you cancel?


Support Who answers when a form fills wrong, and how fast?


## Run a pilot on one real account


1. Pick a messy renewal: scanned dec pages, a loss run, an MVR, a vehicle spreadsheet and last year’s ACORD 125.
2. Pick the lines and forms you would actually send to a market.
3. Check ten hard fields: FEIN, class codes, five years of losses, three VINs, year built and square footage.
4. Count the values you had to look up yourself, and whether each one showed its source.
5. Decide whether you would send the PDF without retyping it. That is the test that matters.
